finding: Earlier recovery/client-leak claim was incorrect: the prepatch require_principal already rejected recovery cookies, and its local is_api_client branch rejected bearers. No prepatch GET/client bypass was substantiated.
patch: Defensive consolidation onto existing require_browser_session, preserving prior normal-browser-only behavior; additional actual recovery-cookie and normal-browser positive-control regression assertions.

reviewed_private_auth_gets.GET/api/client: Prior require_principal excluded recovery and local is_api_client branch excluded bearers. Shared browser helper retains both boundaries.
reviewed_private_auth_gets.GET/auth/sessions/whoami: Existing normal-browser guard, no recovery identity.
reviewed_private_auth_gets.GET/api/auth/check: Recovery returns only reset capability and empty roles/permissions; no personal DB projection. Normal browser receives authorized private projection; API bearer denied.
reviewed_private_auth_gets.GET/auth/self-service/settings/browser a: Only session-bound normal browser or explicitly restricted recovery password flow; recovery nodes omit identity traits.
reviewed_private_auth_gets.Other browser flow creation/reads: Recovery denied outside settings; logout may revoke its own limited capability and returns no personal projection. Browser-bound flow-error returns generic flow error only.
reviewed_private_auth_gets.Verification/recovery token redemption: Unexpired delivered one-time hashed capability, not a private account projection; recovery issues reset-only cookie.

acceptance_source: Genuine mail-delivered recovery cookie and actual normal-browser client creation/list positive control; supported private GET/client,user/follows/manga,whoami must deny recovery without client metadata. GET/settings is not a supported route and is not counted as authorization evidence.
